about.title: Delano Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often in the time it takes to walk through a wet entryway or across a cracked parking lot near Cecil Avenue or High Street. What follows can be a slower, more frustrating process: medical visits, missed shifts, and a property owner or their insurer who isn't eager to take responsibility. California premises liability law asks whether the property owner or manager knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and did nothing to fix or warn about it. That's why what happens in the hours and days after your fall matters so much. Photos of the hazard, incident reports, and store surveillance footage can disappear or get overwritten if no one asks for them. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent Delano-area attorney who can start gathering that evidence and explain your options before time runs short.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Property Owner's Insurer Calls

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: Under California law, you generally must show the property owner or manager knew, or should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, complaint history, and inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Delano businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can be critical to showing how and why the fall happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that reflects your actual role, if any, in what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Delano?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a Kern County building or sidewalk, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim, so it's worth getting advice quickly.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Garces Highway and no one gave me an incident report?
items.answer: You can still pursue a claim without one, though it helps your case. An attorney can request the store's internal records, employee statements, and any video footage separately, since businesses along corridors like Garces Highway and High Street often keep their own incident logs even if you weren't given a copy.

items.question: Will I have to prove the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Generally, yes, California premises liability law requires showing the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition. This can be shown through prior complaints, how long the hazard existed, or evidence that routine inspections were skipped.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, our service is free to use. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
